title.narrative: Improving China¿s institutional capacity towards universal social protection (Phase 2)

description.narrative:
The overall objective is to support the reform of China¿s national policies regarding social standards, including the strengthening of its social protection system and its alignment with international standards.

This will also enhance the EU-China dialogues and cooperation on employment, social affairs and inclusion, in line with the external dimension of European Pillar of Social Rights and its action plan (2021) and the Commission¿s Communication on Decent Work Worldwide (2022).

comment.narrative: In September 2023 the Project supported five Chinese participants 1 woman and 4 men from tripartite constituents namely MOHRSS AllChina Federation of Trade Unions ACFTU and China Enterprise Confederation CEC and from National Healthcare Security Administration NHSA to attend the Academy on Social Security a twoweeks indepth international training programme on comprehensive Social Protection organized by the International Training Centre of the ILO in Turin Italy. In November 2023 the Project organized a first Tripartite Dialogue session on the Future of Social Security where 11 participants 4 women and 7 men from tripartite partners defined three main priorities to improve the performance of the social security system in China in the coming 3 to 5 years.

comment.narrative: 5 participants 1 woman and 4 men for Academy on Social Security and 11 4 women and 7 men for the meeting on future of social security. It shall be noted that instead of the initial target of 30 participants the project prioritized a more targeted audience with relevant departments of tripartite partners regarding the technical workshop organized in November 2023 to discuss and define three common priority areas requiring ILO technical support to improve the performance of social security system in China in the coming 3 to 5 years under the Future of Social Security dialogue. For such a purpose a smaller scale meeting of 11 participants from relevant departments of tripartite partners would better contribute to a focused scoping of common actions through dynamic interactions that engaged everyone.
